title: Max Plays Four Square
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: At recess, Max wants to play four square. There is a big square painted on the blacktop.
The big square has four little squares inside. One kid stands in each square.
The kid in the top square serves the ball. The ball must bounce one time in your square, and then you hit it to another square.
If the ball bounces two times, or goes out, you are out. Then you go to the back of the line.
Max gets in line and waits. Waiting is hard! Max wiggles and wiggles.
Finally, it is Max's turn. The ball comes fast. Max hits it with two paws. Bonk! It goes into Kai's square.
Kai hits it back. Max hits it again. Max moves up and up, all the way to the top square!
Then Max hits the ball too hard. It flies out. Max is out. "That's okay," says Kai. "Good game!"
Max goes to the back of the line, smiling. Max can not wait to play again.

quiz.q: How many times can the ball bounce in your square?
quiz.ev: The ball must bounce one time in your square

quiz.q: Why did Max smile after getting out?
o: The game was fun and Kai was kind

quiz.q: What does "serves" mean in this game?
o: Starts the game by hitting the ball
quiz.ev: The kid in the top square serves the ball.
